channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: November 2026 All Media Show · Crossroads Art Center
item.description: Crossroads Art Center in Richmond represents more than 300 artists and runs a bimonthly juried call with cash awards of $100 for first place, $75 for second and $50 for third. The November edition has no theme — it is an open juried show judged by a guest juror drawn from the Richmond arts community (a gallery director, curator, museum official, arts professor or accomplished artist), shown live in the gallery and simultaneously online. This cycle's juror had not been named at the time of listing. Photography sits in the organiser's own eligible-media list alongside painting, mixed media, collage, fiber, sculpture, ceramics, glass, digital art, woodworking and assemblage. NOTE THE WINDOW: entries are only accepted from 1 to 18 October 2026, so the portal is not open yet — the gallery routes submissions through a per-show artcall.org subdomain and has not yet published the November one, which will be linked from crossroadsartcenter.com/pages/call-for-entries when the call opens. Entry is $15 per submission for the general public with a limit of three, or $12 per submission for gallery members who also get a fourth entry free. The gallery accepts only original work by the entering artist, and requires that artists use their own photographic references: AI-generated images, professionally photographed images by another person, another artist's images and instructor's images are all strictly prohibited, with a two-year ban for violations. Artists are notified by 23 October, drop-off runs 11 to 14 November by noon, the exhibition opens on Friday 20 November from 5 to 8 pm and closes on 3 January 2027, with work collected from 5 January. Commission on sales is 30%. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $15 per work ($12 members). Prize: $100 + exhibition.

item.title: Neoteric Abstract XV · Limner Gallery
item.description: SlowArt Productions' fifteenth Neoteric Abstract exhibition at Limner Gallery in Hudson, New York is built for the abstract artist alone, and sets out to represent the full range of abstraction — from the geometric to the lyrical, from the precise to the raw. Photography is named in the organiser's own list of eligible media alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, graphics, digital and installation art and video, and the only content restriction is that the work be abstract; entrants must be 18 or older, and the call is open nationally and internationally. Wall-mounted work must be no taller than 72 inches and no wider than 120 inches, and sculpture must fit through a 36-inch door. Video may be entered by supplying a link to a file hosted on Vimeo, YouTube or a similar platform, with each link counting as one image. Entry is by email, with four works covered by the fee and further works at $5 each; details of a two-dimensional work count as an additional entry, though sculptors may add one extra view per piece at no cost. Artists accepted to exhibit pay nothing further. Selected artists are shown at Limner Gallery from 15 April to 8 May 2027, with the exhibition also carried on the gallery's website and promoted on social media. Work may be exhibited for sale or not for sale at prices the artist sets, and the gallery takes a 35% commission on sales. Results are posted at slowart.com/results no later than 28 February 2027, and that posting — not the email — is the official notification. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: $35 (up to 4 works), $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Into the Light: Third Annual Darkroom Members Exhibition · The Halide Project
item.description: The Halide Project is a nonprofit darkroom and gallery on North 2nd Street in Philadelphia, and its Darkroom Members Exhibition is the annual show of what has come out of that darkroom: work made by current Halide darkroom members, plus anything produced in one of the organisation's workshops. The medium gate is the same strict one the organisation applies to its flagship Living Image call — work must be made using traditional, pre-digital photographic printing, including but not limited to silver gelatin, c-prints, instant film, platinum/palladium, cyanotype, gum bichromate, wet plate collodion and other alternative and historic processes. Analog prints made from digital negatives are eligible; inkjet prints and digital c-prints are not. One submission per person, framed work no larger than 16 by 20 inches including the frame, and the application is a short Airtable form asking about the work and the maker. There is no entry fee. Everything included in the exhibition is published in a printed catalogue. Accepted work must be dropped off at The Halide Project by 4 October — delivery is assumed to be in person, though the organisation will discuss shipping by email — and must stay up for the full run. The show opens with a reception on Saturday 10 October from 5 to 8 pm and is on view to 5 December 2026. Artists keep their copyright, grant promotional use, and the gallery retains a 25% commission on sales. — Deadline: September 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Printed catalogue.

item.title: REWIND. PIVOT. REPEAT. · Shemer Art Center
item.description: The Shemer Art Center & Museum in Phoenix devotes this juried group show to the idea that life rarely follows a straight path — that we revisit old ideas, rediscover forgotten memories and adapt, and that looking back is often how transformation starts. Artists are invited to work from nostalgia, history, personal milestones, cultural evolution, adaptation, resilience and renewal, drawing on specific eras, family histories, traditions, architecture, fashion, music or the pivotal moments that redirected a life. Original works in all visual media are welcome and photography is named explicitly alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, fiber, mixed media, glass and digital art; photographic entries must state how the work will be printed and displayed, whether framed under glass, on metal or otherwise. The juror is Bentley Calverley, who founded Bentley Gallery in 1984 and spent a career introducing leading-edge contemporary art to Scottsdale and Phoenix. Entrants must be Arizona residents aged 18 or over, work must have been made within the last three years and cannot have been shown at the Shemer before, and nothing may exceed five feet high by four feet wide. Up to three works may be entered, at $40 for one rising to $50 for three, with member rates of $30 to $40. Notification is on 2 October, hand-delivered work is due on 23 October between 1 and 4 pm, and the exhibition runs from 28 October 2026 to 7 January 2027 with an artist reception on 29 October from 5:30 to 7:30 pm. All work is insured by the Center, artists keep 70% of any sale, and accepted artists agree to help with installation and promotion. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $40 for 1 work, $50 for 3 ($30–$40 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Strange Weather · Art Center Sarasota
item.description: Art Center Sarasota's Atrium Gallery show for autumn 2026 celebrates the surreal, inviting artists into worlds where reality bends, logic dissolves and the unexpected becomes possible. 'Weather' here is a metaphor rather than a subject: submissions may read it as environmental, emotional or psychological, catching the moment when the familiar turns strange, and the call asks for dreamlike imagery, psychological landscapes, improbable juxtapositions, transformation and ambiguity. Submissions are welcome in all media including photography, and AI-generated art is not allowed. The juror is Danny Canton, a veteran of more than fifty years in the film industry who has worked as a director, producer and most often as a director of photography, and who studied cinematography at the School of Visual Arts before building the online film programme at Full Sail University. Jurying is done blind — the juror sees everything except the artist's name and the price — and the awards are chosen in person once the show is hung: $500 for first place, $300 for second, $200 for third, plus two merit awards and four honourable mentions. Up to three works may be entered; two-dimensional work may not exceed 72 by 65 inches framed. Note a date conflict on the organiser's own surfaces: the Submittable form's text says Sunday 6 September while the Art Center's website and the portal's own closing time both give Monday 7 September, so aim for 6 September to be safe. All work must be offered for sale — no NFS or price-on-request — and the artist receives 60% of the selling price as a member or 50% as a non-member. Artists are notified by 16 September, work is received in person on 29 and 30 September or by post by 30 September, and the show runs 8 October to 14 November 2026 with an opening reception on 8 October from 5 to 7 pm. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: $40 for 1 work, $65 for 3 ($30–$45 members, $10–$35 students). Prize: $500 + exhibition.

item.title: The Short List · Cultural Council for Palm Beach County
item.description: The Cultural Council for Palm Beach County fills its Lake Worth Beach gallery with small work once a year and sells it, and The Short List is built around the idea that a first purchase should be possible: an exhibition of tiny pieces pitched at collectors of every kind, from people buying their first artwork to people adding to a collection. Artists working in all styles and media, two- and three-dimensional, are welcome, and the Council's suggested directions — collage, abstract, whimsical, flora and fauna, food — are subjects rather than a medium list. Every work must be no greater than 12 inches framed in its longest dimension, with no minimum size, and the Council asks artists to price at or below $500 because that is what sells in this show, while explicitly not excluding higher prices. Up to three completed individual works may be submitted, one entry per artist, and sets such as diptychs and triptychs are not accepted — pieces may complement each other but must be priced and sold separately. Entry is free and applications are taken only through Artwork Archive, where a free account is enough to apply. Artists are accepted on a rolling basis up to a cap of 150 participants, so applying early matters, and everyone hears by 5 November. Selected artists deliver and collect their own work on dates coordinated with the Council, sign a memorandum of understanding and a loan agreement, and the Council retains 25% of sales to fund its artist services staff and the building. The exhibition itself opens on 12 March 2027, five months after the deadline. Work is insured on the premises but not in transit. — Deadline: October 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 61st CAIN National · Del Mar College
item.description: An open-theme, all-media national juried exhibition at Del Mar College's Joseph A. Cain Memorial Gallery in Corpus Christi, founded in 1966 and formerly the Annual National Drawing & Small Sculpture Show — renamed to reflect a broader range of media. Photography is named among the accepted 2-D categories alongside drawing, painting, printmaking in traditional media and original watercolor; sculpture of any media is also considered, though nothing requiring ceiling suspension. $10,000 in Purchase Awards are decided by the juror and the college art faculty, and purchased work joins Del Mar's permanent collection. This year's juror is Jamie Bates, a ceramic artist and Associate Professor of Ceramics at the University of Oklahoma, who also gives a free public art talk on February 18. Open to artists residing in the United States, excluding full-time Del Mar art faculty; work must have been created in the last three years and must not have been shown previously in the Annual Show. Each artist may submit three works, one image per artwork. Entries open on CaFÉ on September 1, 2026 and close November 30, 2026; notification goes out January 8, 2027, accepted work must arrive by January 30, and the exhibition runs February 19 – April 19, 2027. Work does not have to be for sale — the gallery publishes a price list and connects artists with buyers but takes no other part in sales — and artists are responsible for all return shipping costs. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $20 (2 entries) + $5 each additional. Prize: $10,000 in purchase awards.

item.title: Art Omi: Artists Residency 2027
item.description: A three-and-a-half-week summer residency on Art Omi's 300-acre campus in New York's Hudson Valley, gathering roughly two dozen international artists to work, collaborate and share ideas. Residents are given a private bedroom in shared living quarters, a private studio and three meals a day at no cost, and are responsible for their own travel and materials unless eligible for one of the fellowship travel grants. Two critics or curators join each session as Critics-in-Residence, leading discussions and making individual studio visits, while the Visitors Program brings critics, curators, gallerists and established artists to the campus; the session ends with a public Open Studios event. Facilities include indoor and protected outdoor studios, a kiln and basic hand tools, with professional colour photography labs in nearby Ghent. Open to artists anywhere in the world who have been professionally active for at least the past five years — disciplines include visual arts, sound art, performance and social practice, and having studied art is not a requirement, though a CV must show five years of practice. Current BFA and MFA students are not eligible, nor are past Art Omi residents; applicants must be 18 or over, submitted work must date from the past ten years, and applications must be written in English. Several fellowships add stipends of $500 to $2,000 plus travel grants, flagged inside the same application and in some cases awarded automatically to every eligible artist, among them the American Dream Fellowship for an artist who has never been to the United States, the Every Page Foundation Fellowship for a female artist from an underserved community, and the Unlimit Art Fellowship for artists with disabilities. Artists legally resident in Australia, the Basque Country or Croatia are told by the application form to use their own dedicated fellowship calls instead, while the residency page says they may enter both pools, which separate panels review. In 2026, 24 artists attended out of 1,395 applicants, and Art Omi aims for roughly 75% of residents to come from outside the US. Applications close September 14, 2026, decisions are sent January 1, 2027, and the session runs June 17 – July 12, 2027. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Funded residency.

item.title: Portsmouth Open 26 · Photo Fringe
item.description: A new curated group exhibition at Art Space, Portsmouth, staged as part of Photo Fringe 2026 by the volunteer-led Brighton photography charity behind the biennial open-platform festival. The show reads archives as feedback loops — how photographs, documents, objects, memories and stories are continually revisited, reinterpreted and reshaped — and looks for artists whose practice engages with personal, family, community, institutional, cultural, historical, digital or found archives, or that questions what constitutes an archive at all. Rephotography, appropriation, collage, installation, moving image, sound and text are all welcomed, and existing or new work may be submitted provided the relationship to the curatorial premise is clear. Open to photographers and lens-based artists working in any medium; solo artists and collectives may both apply. There are no submission fees. Apply by email with up to 300 words — or a BSL, English audio or video application of no more than three minutes — up to 12 JPEGs (72 dpi, each under 3MB) or a screener link for moving image, and a website or Instagram link. Selected artists print and provide their own work with suitable hanging options, install and de-install with support from the Photo Fringe team, and contribute to the invigilation timetable; Photo Fringe takes 35% commission on sales to help cover staffing, and travel, transport and accommodation cannot be reimbursed unless otherwise agreed. Applications are assessed by Photo Fringe producer Ricardo Reverón Blanco, who also selects one artist from the exhibiting cohort for a jury award of mentorship plus an in-depth written interview published on the Photo Fringe website. Entries close 8 September 2026, the shortlist is notified 15 September, the private view is 23 October and the exhibition runs 24–25 October 2026, during the 2–31 October festival. — Deadline: September 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Mentorship.

item.title: 2027 Workspace Artist Residency · Center for Book Arts
item.description: Center for Book Arts awards up to four New York-based emerging and mid-career artists a six-month keyholder residency running April to September 2027, inviting them to explore the book as a time-based medium — "a sequence of spaces, each space perceived at a different moment", in Ulises Carrión's phrase — and as a tool for political engagement, since printmaking and independent publishing have long been central to social and cultural transformation. Residents receive 24/7 keyholder access to shared studio space for six months, a $1,500 honorarium, a $500 material stipend, storage space, basic supplies and tools, free classes in bookbinding, letterpress and RISO, consultations and professional development with staff and visiting curators, scheduled site visits to partner institutions working with artists' books and publishing, support from volunteers, access to Materials for the Arts, and opportunities to present work in exhibitions and public programs. Applications are reviewed blind by an independent panel of arts professionals from a broad range of backgrounds. The program promotes experimentation in book arts and artists from all disciplinary backgrounds are encouraged to apply — CBA aims for a balanced cohort of experienced book artists and artists working in other disciplines with a clear interest in exploring the field. Applications ask for an artist statement and CV, a portfolio of work samples, and a brief proposal naming the projects you would pursue and the equipment, tools and classes at CBA that most interest you. Housing is not provided. The selection panel meets in early October, shortlisted artists are interviewed virtually in mid-October, residencies begin in April 2027, and residents present their work in an artist talk at the end of the program and take part in a group exhibition in 2029. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + $2,000.

item.title: Fellowship Program 2027–2028 · Gallery Route One
item.description: Gallery Route One, the artist-run nonprofit in Point Reyes Station on the Marin coast, is offering two 24-month Fellowships running January 2027 to December 2028 to artists aged 21 to 40. Each Fellow receives a minimum of ten exhibition opportunities — including a solo exhibition in the Annex Gallery in 2027 and a two-person exhibition in the Center Gallery in 2028 — plus a $1,500 stipend to support the production and presentation of that work, mentoring and assistance producing the exhibitions, publicity and promotion, ongoing exposure on GRO's website and social media, and access to all GRO-sponsored professional development. Fellows also become eligible to be hired as Teaching Artists in GRO's Artists in the Schools programme, and work alongside the gallery's practising artist members curating and installing solo and group shows; GRO's call page adds that Fellows “do some volunteer work” during the fellowship period. Applicants must be aged 21 to 40, live and work in the greater Bay Area within commuting distance of Point Reyes Station, have a serious fine arts practice built on training, education and/or experience, and hold a cohesive portfolio of work completed within the last five years together with a developing focus or current area of inquiry and experimentation. GRO has run the Fellowship since 2014, and photography sits comfortably inside it — one past Fellow describes using the two years for a large-scale photography and oral history project, and the gallery separately runs a standing Latino Photography Project. The application asks for 8 to 10 images with dimensions in the filenames, an artist statement referencing two or three of them, a description of your studio practice, a CV and one reference, and it carries no entry fee. Applications are accepted only between 1 and 30 September 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,500 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Access/VSA Emerging Young Artists Program 2027: Thrive · The Kennedy Center
item.description: Thrive is the 2027 edition of the Kennedy Center's Access/VSA Emerging Young Artists Program, a Jean Kennedy Smith Arts and Disability Program that runs as a juried career development programme and exhibition for visual artists with disabilities aged 16 to 25 who live in the United States. The theme asks disabled artists to consider how their life and their art are flourishing: how the work is evolving and changing, and how the person is developing and growing. Fifteen artists are selected by a jury of industry professionals; each receives a $3,000 stipend and has one of their submitted pieces included in an exhibit in Washington, D.C. Winners are required to attend three virtual workshops (3 April, 1 May and 5 June 2027) and an all-expenses-paid series of career development workshops in Washington from 14 to 18 June 2027. Entry is free. All visual art forms and media are eligible if they meet the handling rules — 2D work no larger than 60 inches in height or width, 3D no larger than 48 inches in any direction when packed, nothing perishable — and work must have been completed in the last three years and after the onset of disability. Applicants submit images or video of at least three different pieces, and are told to show a portfolio rather than several views of one work, alongside four 300-word answers on themselves, their process, the perspective they would bring and their future plans. Previous programme winners cannot reapply, group projects are not considered, and artwork created with generative AI is ineligible. Selected applicants are asked to document their disability, age and right to work in the US before the final round, and must be willing to publicly disclose that they have a disability in all materials and public appearances associated with the programme. Accommodations and alternate application formats can be requested until 30 October 2026. The submission portal opens on 24 August. — Deadline: November 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,000 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Open Door: 2027 Exhibition & Residency · Kinhouse Gallery
item.description: Open Door is Kinhouse's annual call for its next programming year, and the 2027 round wants exhibition proposals from emerging and mid-career artists and curators — solo, two- and three-person shows, collaborations, artist collectives, performances, installations and site-specific work, as well as proposals from curators wanting to organise a show in the space. Three or four proposals are selected by Kinhouse Director Kaylan Buteyn, and every chosen exhibition is paired with a fully funded six-night residency at the Kinhouse Residency, a three-bedroom house with a detached studio a three-minute drive from the gallery, timed so that the opening reception falls on the Friday of the residency week. Shows then hang for the month following that First Friday opening and are promoted through the gallery's channels, its newsletter and the Broadway Arts District's First Friday programming, with professional documentation provided and installation support on site. All art mediums are accepted for consideration, though video and screen-based submissions may require extra support, and work samples may be works in progress or ideas still waiting to be developed rather than finished pieces. The gallery says it is especially drawn to work engaging community, care, belonging, the domestic, parenting, craft and lineage — the values that shape its programme — but proposals do not have to sit inside that scope. Entry is $34 for one proposal and up to three proposals may be submitted. Work does not have to be for sale, though it is preferred; selected artists sign an exhibition contract with a 20% gallery commission, paid out within two weeks of the show closing. The call is open internationally, but Kinhouse cannot cover travel or shipping, and artists ship work both ways unless it sells. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $34. Prize: Exhibition + fully funded six-night residency.

item.title: Solo Exhibition at Gallery VERY
item.description: Gallery VERY, which describes itself as one of Boston's longest-running independent artist-run galleries, is looking for one artist to give a five-week solo exhibition in its 500-square-foot space in the SoWa arts district. No exhibition proposal is required — the gallery says it is selecting an artist, not a pre-planned exhibition, and Gallery Director John Guthrie will then work with the selected artist to develop a show for the space roughly six months after selection, with new work considered as the exhibition takes shape. Photography is named alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, mixed media, installation, video and interdisciplinary practices, and there are no restrictions on age, education, career stage or professional status. The gallery provides professional installation, an opening reception, a public artist talk, promotion, sales representation for the run of the show, and a permanent exhibition page on its website; sales are split 50/50, the artist covers transport both ways, and work is not insured by the gallery. Applications ask for 8–10 work samples that show a broad picture of your current practice (video artists may send 2–3 clips of up to three minutes with stills), a 200-word statement, a 100-word bio and a two-page CV. Location eligibility is regional: artists must live and work within approximately 250 miles of Boston, and the selected artist is expected to be present in person for the opening and the talk. VERY marks ten years in 2026 and presents four to five exhibitions a year. The CaFE portal opens on 24 August. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Five-week solo exhibition.

item.title: Chasing Ghosts 10: Piercing the Veil through Remembrance, Legacy & Beyond · Verum Ultimum Art Gallery
item.description: The tenth edition of Chasing Ghosts, the series Verum Ultimum's director conceived when the Portland gallery was celebrating its third year and describes as a favourite with artists and collectors alike. This year's edition is virtual. The emphasis, as always, is the idea of revealing the unseen, and “ghost” is not meant to be read literally — the gallery suggests this round's interpretations might be loaded with the added turmoil of the current social, health, environmental and political climate. It asks whether you express your deepest fears or concerns through your work, what parts of the past leave their mark on it, whether a legacy is revealed through your work or your process, and whether memory is a vital vehicle of expression for you. Any interpretation of the call is encouraged, and all mediums and modes of expression are welcome. Entry is $25 covering two images, with additional images at $5 each up to six; applicants must be 18 or older and the call is open internationally. Selected work is shown in Verum's virtual viewing galleries, which display work at scale, and carried through an exhibition book, an exhibition page, the website at large and blog posts, with social media promotion staying on the show for four weeks. Work may be listed for sale or entered as exhibition-only; the gallery takes a 30% commission on sales, provides prepaid shipping labels when work sells, and allows no substitutions of accepted work. The exhibition opens in mid-October and runs for a month. — Deadline: September 22, 2026. Fee: $25 (2 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition + catalogue.

item.title: Small Art, Big Impact · Blaine Arts Council
item.description: Blaine Art Gallery, on Peace Portal Drive in the Washington border town of Blaine, asks artists to make a powerful statement within a compact format for this national juried exhibition. Two-dimensional work may be no larger than 16 inches on its longest side including the frame; three-dimensional work no larger than 15 inches in height, width or depth. There is no restriction on theme or subject — the gallery invites realistic, abstract and unexpected approaches, and says artistry, content and composition rather than sheer scale should command attention. Photography is explicitly on the accepted-media list alongside painting, mixed media, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics, jewellery, fibre arts and digital art; video, film, audio, giclee prints and installations are not eligible, and neither are reproductions of work made under an instructor's close direction or work generated by AI. Entrants must reside in the US and may submit one to three works. All accepted work must be for sale, with the gallery retaining a 25% commission plus tax, and 2D work must be wired with no wires showing. Shipping in both directions is the artist's responsibility, though the gallery insures accepted work for the duration of the exhibit. The show runs 10 October to 8 November 2026 with an opening reception on 10 October from 4 to 6.30pm; acceptances go out on 20 September. No juror is named and no cash awards are listed. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art In The Making · Gallery Route One
item.description: The annual juried exhibition of Gallery Route One, the 501(c)(3) non-profit in Point Reyes Station whose stated mission is to originate and present contemporary art exhibitions, educational programs and community outreach. The 2027 edition runs 9 January to 13 February, with a reception and awards on Saturday 9 January from 3 to 5pm. Mike Grady, a Bay Area painter, writer and educator, is the juror, and will select six artists for awards. Jurying is blind and done from the digital images submitted; any contact with the juror by an applicant during the process automatically disqualifies the artist. All media are accepted except video, crafts and installation, and no work may exceed 48 inches in any direction. Entry is $20 per artwork, up to a maximum of four entries, and eligibility is limited to artists currently living in Northern California. Accepted work must be clean, framed, wired and ready to hang or place on a base, and labelled on the back with the artist's details, title, medium, dimensions and price. Work is hand-delivered on 3 or 4 January or shipped at the artist's expense in a returnable two-way carton — work packed in styrofoam or not prepaid for return will not be accepted — and the gallery does not insure work in the gallery or in transit. Work is for sale unless marked NFS, with a 45% commission to be included in the price and a note on whether the frame is included. Notification is emailed in the first week of December 2026. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: $20 per work (up to 4). Prize: Exhibition + six juror awards.

item.title: Open Theme 2026 · The Lab on Santa Fe
item.description: An all-media open call from The Lab on Santa Fe, the gallery at 840 Santa Fe Drive that sits in the middle block of Denver's Art District on Santa Fe, where the gallery says the First Friday Art Walk pulls the largest crowds in the state. “Open theme” means no theme: the organisers want artists to take control and test what the space can hold, and they name photographers alongside painters, illustrators, printmakers, sculptors, video artists, installation artists, collage and assemblage artists, textile and fibre artists and ceramists. Nature, humanity, politics, chaos, transcendence — whatever pulls at you. They ask to feel the rigour inside your process, saying risk, intensity and the possibility of failure are all part of the atmosphere, but are emphatic that this is not meant to exclude anyone: all mediums, all styles, all subject matter, the only rule being to show you are open to your muse rather than trying to please. Entry is $34 for one or two works and one application per artist. Location eligibility is listed as national rather than Colorado-only. All submitted art must be for sale, measurements on applications must be accurate, and work can be turned away at drop-off for improper wiring; sales are split 58% to the artist and 42% to the gallery. The exhibition runs 5 to 27 February 2027. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $34. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Beyond the Image Art Prize 2026 · Via Gluck 62 AIR
item.description: Via Gluck 62 AIR, a non-profit cultural association with its own space on via Gluck in Milan, has launched the first edition of the Beyond the Image Art Prize, an international open call for contemporary photography, video art, experimental film, moving images and hybrid or installation-based practices that use photographic and audiovisual language. Its full title is "Who Are You Beyond the Image? Art, Neuroscience and Algorithmic Narration of Experience", and it grows out of SatisFace, a research project on the face, self-image perception and the neuroscientific, psychological and cultural implications of representing identity. The prize wants work that reflects on identity, image, body perception, digital technology and the algorithmic narration of experience, read through documentary, conceptual, poetic, critical or installation approaches. Two projects are selected, one by an emerging artist and one by an established artist, and each gets a solo exhibition in the association's Milan space plus a place in the official programme of the Milano Centrale Festival 2026, curatorial and organisational support, promotion, and a possible contribution towards production costs agreed with the artist. Entry is open to any nationality with no age, education or career requirements, and collectives may apply. Applicants send a project proposal of up to 2,500 characters with up to five supporting images, a CV and a portfolio, all under 25 MB total. The €19 fee is paid by bank transfer. The exhibition runs 2–30 October 2026, opening during the festival. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: €19. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Prix Yzza Slaoui de la Découverte · Rencontres de la Photographie Marrakech
item.description: The Rencontres de la Photographie de Marrakech has created a new prize in memory of Yzza Slaoui, aimed at revealing and supporting one Moroccan photographer whose work shows a personal vision and real artistic quality. The theme is free. The winning project earns a solo exhibition or an official projection inside the 2027 festival programme plus a €2,000 cash award decided by the international jury — and, importantly, the festival covers production, printing, framing, transport and installation separately, so none of that comes out of the €2,000. Entry is free and open exclusively to photographers of Moroccan nationality who own the rights to the images; the project must be unpublished in Morocco, or at least never have had a solo exhibition there. No age limit applies, though the prize is aimed first at emerging photographers. Applicants send a body of 15 to 30 photographs in a chosen, numbered sequence, at a resolution good for a 30 cm print, together with a two-page statement of intent, a CV, a ten-line biography and proof of Moroccan nationality. Dossiers may be written in French or English, and one project per photographer. A first selection is made by the festival's artistic committee before the international jury deliberates on 9 October 2026. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €2,000 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Artist Residency Program · The Art Center
item.description: The Art Center in Dover, New Hampshire gives three artists a four-month studio residency in its space at the Washington Street Mills, and thanks to a local benefactor it costs the selected artists nothing — the gallery values the opportunity at $2,500. This round covers 1 October through 31 January. Residents get their own studio with a shared utility sink and are asked to be there twenty hours a week, drawing on downtown Dover, the Cocheco river and the Seacoast arts scene, and to build a body of work that goes up in the Artist Residency Exhibition in the gallery at the end of the term. Residents also help coordinate two artists' receptions and hang one exhibit during the term. This is studio space only; housing is not included, so it suits artists already within reach of the Seacoast. Applicants must be 18 or older and pay a $25 application fee, plus a $100 damage deposit returned at the end of the residency. The gallery takes 30 percent commission on work sold from the exhibition, and artists keep full rights to their images. Applications go through a form on the gallery's own site, with five examples of work, a CV and two character references sent by email. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Studio residency + exhibition.

item.title: The Truth about Cats and Dogs · Not Shockboxx
item.description: Not Shockboxx is a queer-owned gallery in Hermosa Beach that describes itself as artist-forward and built for work that does not fit neatly inside traditional systems. This call is for its online programme: artwork about the creatures we live with, admire, rescue, fear or simply cannot stop thinking about. The brief is deliberately wide — domestic, wild, mythical or microscopic, anything with fur, feathers, scales, shells, tentacles, hooves, wings or too many legs — and the gallery is explicit that cute is optional and weird is encouraged. Photography is named among the accepted media alongside painting, sculpture, fiber, ceramics, printmaking, assemblage and video. Selected artists are shown in a two-month exhibition on Artsy, where the gallery is a partner, running 1 September to 31 October 2026. Entry is $20 per artwork with up to three works per artist, and the gallery says it cares about the work rather than the résumé, education, exhibition history or follower count. Artists 18 and over anywhere in the world may apply where they can meet shipping requirements. All accepted work must be priced for sale because Artsy does not permit NFS listings, and artists keep possession unless a piece sells. Work made wholly or partly with generative AI is ineligible. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: $20 per artwork. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: The Good Stuff · Not Shockboxx
item.description: Marking Suicide Prevention and Awareness Month, Not Shockboxx asks artists to notice what makes life worth staying for — not milestones or picture-perfect moments but the smaller, deeply personal things: the first quiet hour of the morning, a perfectly made cup of coffee, the particular way sunlight enters a room, a dog asleep at your feet, an inside joke, a song played a thousand times. The gallery is clear that a submitted piece does not need to address suicide or mental health directly; this call is about the other side of that conversation. Work can be joyful, tender, funny, strange, nostalgic, imperfect or almost impossible to explain, and the organisers suggest you may already have made it without realising where it belonged. All media and approaches are welcome, and the exhibition runs online through Artsy from 21 September to 20 November 2026 so audiences beyond the Hermosa Beach gallery can see it. Entry is $20; gallery artists and Backboxx Artist Society members apply free. Not Shockboxx welcomes work that is provocative, political, sexual, unsettling, profane or experimental, and it does not accept work made wholly or partly with generative AI. Accepted work must be priced for sale, since Artsy will not list NFS pieces. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: The Food We Share · Schack Art Center
item.description: Schack Art Center in Everett, Washington runs an annual Arts Education in Action exhibition, and for 2027 it wants work about food in its broadest sense: culture, family, connection, recipes, ritual, aesthetics, agriculture, nutrition, nostalgia, evolution, insecurity, comfort, entertainment and art. The prompt is unusually well built out, with strands the gallery lists as cooking and eating, science, connection and symbolism, harvest, industry, survival and power — the last of which points at food insecurity, food deserts, food waste, gender roles and class divisions. Photography is named explicitly among the media sought, next to painting, drawing, sculpture, furniture, printmaking, fiber, glass and video, and installation proposals are encouraged. Out of respect for those facing food insecurity the gallery discourages work made of food, and every accepted artist is asked to supply a favourite recipe for a booklet visitors take home. The call is open to artists living and working in the Pacific Northwest; entry is $5, with up to six pieces per artist, and work must not have shown at Schack before. Accepted pieces hang in the Main and Mezzanine Galleries from 25 March to 22 May 2027. All work must be for sale for the run of the show and Schack takes 40 percent. Nothing made in whole or part by AI is accepted. — Deadline: January 24, 2027. Fee: $5 per artist. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Small Works 2026 · Georgetown Art Center
item.description: The Georgetown Art Center, run by the City of Georgetown's Arts and Culture programme in the town's historic district north of Austin, holds an annual juried exhibition of work no larger than twelve inches in any direction. Each piece has to distil a full artistic vision into a compact format, and the hang is designed for close looking. Entries may be in any media, 2-D or 3-D, abstract or representational; photography and digital entries are explicitly invited, and camera-generated photographs, computer-enhanced digital images, digital collage or montage and digital and graphic design may all be entered, so long as the output is framed or mounted with hanging hardware and stays inside the twelve-inch limit. Only original work is accepted, and reproductions and giclee copies of other artworks are not. Artists may enter up to three pieces, of which one will be shown if selected. Work must have been made between January 2023 and the closing date and must be for sale; the centre keeps a 30 per cent commission. Entries are scored online by the Georgetown Art Center Exhibits Committee, with the guest judge choosing the awards. Selected work may be hand-delivered or shipped with a prepaid return label. The show runs 20 November 2026 to 3 January 2027, with a reception and prize-giving on 21 November. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 works). Prize: $500 Best of Show; $300, $200, $100, $50.

item.title: 62nd Annual Open Juried Art Competition · Anaheim Art Association
item.description: The Anaheim Art Association has run an open juried competition every year since the 1960s, and for the 62nd edition it again partners with the MuzeO Museum and Cultural Center, showing the selected work in the museum's main gallery in the Carnegie Building in downtown Anaheim. Photography is a judged category in its own right, split into Basic Photography and Manipulated Composite, with its own judge; the other categories are oil, acrylic, watercolour, drawing and pastel, and mixed media. There is no theme and no restriction on when the work was made. Cash awards and honourable mentions are given at the jurors' discretion, and a category is merged into the next smallest if it draws fewer than twelve entries. Work must be original, with no class work, nothing made under instruction and no AI-created or AI-assisted work; no reproductions or giclee copies of another artist's work are accepted, and where a photograph has been used as source material the photographer's written permission is required. Entries are capped at four per artist and at 43 inches in either direction including the frame, and everything must be framed or gallery-wrapped with wire hangers; the MuzeO takes a 30 per cent commission on sales. Note that everyone submitting may be asked either to help at check-in or to sit the gallery for one two-hour shift during the run, and that accepted work is hand-delivered on 6 or 7 November. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $45 first entry, $15 each additional ($35/$10 members). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Exhibition Submissions · Waterworks Visual Arts Center
item.description: Waterworks Visual Arts Center in Salisbury, North Carolina is a non-collecting art museum accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, and it keeps a standing portfolio-review route into its exhibition programme. Each year the museum mounts three major rotating exhibitions of contemporary fine art and craft by local, regional, national and international artists, plus an annual outdoor sculpture show, and its past programme has repeatedly given solo shows to photographers. Submissions are read twice a year, after deadlines on 30 September and 30 January, and are reviewed within sixty to ninety days; the museum is clear that this is review only and not a guarantee of a show. Because the exhibition calendar is planned eighteen to twenty-four months ahead, a successful submission buys real time to prepare or make new work. Applicants send a current CV detailing education, grants, fellowships, awards, teaching, gallery affiliations, major exhibitions and collections, an artist statement written specifically about the body of work submitted and its influences, research, media and concepts, and ten to twenty high-quality images of current work that is available to exhibit, each labelled with title, medium, size, weight and completion date. All work must have been made within the last five years. Everything goes through the museum's SlideRoom portal. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: None listed.

item.title: First Encounter · Kora Art Collective
item.description: Kora Art Collective is a curator-led platform founded in Austin, Texas to show work by emerging and mid-career artists of African descent, working through exhibitions, private sales, cultural programmes and advisory services. First Encounter is a two-part exhibition presented during the Austin Studio Tour, one of the largest art events in Texas, which runs over the weekends of 14-15 and 21-22 November 2026. The collective is calling for work across painting, drawing, prints, photography, sculpture, mixed media and textile and fibre, and will consider selected craft-based work alongside the visual art submissions. Entry is free and open internationally. Artists submit three to ten images of available work, one entry per artist, giving title, year completed, medium, dimensions and price where known, along with an artist statement, CV or bio and a link to a website, portfolio or Instagram. Two-dimensional work cannot exceed 36 by 36 inches; three-dimensional work cannot exceed 24 inches in each direction or 15 pounds. Framing is not required but work must arrive presentable. The exhibition runs 14 November to 6 December 2026. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at Austin Studio Tour.

item.title: Call for Art: 2D Temporary Public Art Installation · Rochester Contemporary Art Center
item.description: RoCo invites artists to propose three images for a temporary public art installation outside its main facility on East Avenue, a twice-yearly call with deadlines on September 15 and March 15. The selected series is printed on weather-safe material at roughly 9 feet high by 6 feet wide and shown to the public 24/7 for four to six months; RoCo covers all production and installation costs and pays the artist a $400 stipend and use fee for exhibiting preexisting images. Files must be vertical and delivered at 12,000 x 8,000 pixels. Of particular interest are projects that connect viewers to the location, community and history of the neighbourhood, that challenge passersby, and that address social and political issues; RoCo welcomes visual artists of all genres and also invites collaborations between visual and literary artists. Open to local, national and international artists, including those who have already exhibited at RoCo, though submissions from Rochester artists may occasionally be given preference. The site is an urban park in downtown Rochester seen by 300 to 600 people a week. Proposals go by email as a single PDF with contact details, a CV, a project proposal of up to 500 words and the three captioned images. Artists are selected by October 15 and April 15. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $400 stipend and use fee.

item.title: Annual Call for Submissions and Exhibition Proposals · Rochester Contemporary Art Center
item.description: Rochester Contemporary Art Center, a not-for-profit founded in 1977, keeps a standing annual open call for general and video submissions toward future exhibition seasons, with a December 31 deadline every year. General submissions take a letter of intent saying what you want to do and what you are open to, whether a curatorial project, a solo show or inclusion in any project the gallery is planning, plus a CV, an artist statement, up to 20 images and an image checklist giving title, date, medium and presentation size for each. Site-specific installation and curated project proposals should carry as much detail as possible in the letter. RoCo names immigration, housing, and artists' rights and censorship as special topics of interest for this cycle. A separate video programme welcomes proposals from curators, artists and organisations worldwide, preferably programmes of several single-channel works curated around a theme, in any form including experimental, documentary, animation, narrative and virtual reality; curators may propose two to five works of up to 20 minutes each, and curated video projects from around the Great Lakes are especially welcome. Materials go through a single online form. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Share Your Immigration Experience · Rochester Contemporary Art Center
item.description: Part of RoCo's larger exhibition Sanctuary: Borders and Belonging in 2026, this call invites immigrants of all ages, backgrounds and geographies to submit one visual artwork expressing or documenting their personal experience of immigration. Artwork may be in any artistic medium or craft. RoCo suggests working from personal narrative and lived experience: stories of arrival, hope, aspiration, belonging, loss, escape or resilience; encounters with systems that criminalise and exclude or that welcome and support; family histories, cultural inheritance and everyday rituals; and responses to border politics, detention or racialised policing. The gallery is explicit that it wants the full spectrum of experience, including immigrations that were straightforwardly positive, and it also welcomes work made in collaboration between immigrants and non-immigrants. Every eligible entry will be displayed, though the submission process still has to be completed so the installation can be planned, and work may be presented anonymously even though the entry form asks for a name. One piece per artist, no larger than 24 by 24 inches and ready to hang, dropped off at RoCo on September 11 or 12. The exhibition runs October 2 to November 14, 2026, with a reception on October 2. RoCo particularly wants voices living or working in the Rochester area. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Tarot and Oracle: The Art of Divination · Perry Lawson Fine Art
item.description: Perry Lawson Fine Art, a contemporary gallery in a historic building in downtown Nyack, New York, invites paintings, drawings, mixed media, collage, photographs, digital art, prints and sculpture related to tarot and oracle for a juried exhibition running November 21, 2026 to January 10, 2027. Photography is named twice in the gallery's own eligibility text. The show treats these works as artworks in their own right rather than as decks, and the gallery says it is looking for creativity, technical skill and compelling imagery and symbolism, with an eye to work that will appeal both to divination enthusiasts and to a wider public. Selection is on technical skill, originality and the ability to convey meaning through symbolism while still functioning as a compelling work of art. Participating artists may additionally offer their own corresponding tarot or oracle decks for consideration for sale during the run. Open to artists 18 and over residing in the United States, and the gallery will review a maximum of 200 submissions before closing the call. The juror is the artist Dannielle Tegeder. The $22 application fee covers up to five pieces and goes toward the juror's honorarium, the entry platform and marketing. Artists ship accepted work to the gallery at their own cost, though shipping is deducted from the gallery's commission if the work sells. The gallery takes 50% commission on sales. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $22 (up to 5 works). Prize: None listed.

item.title: International Photography Open Call — Edition 3 · Chennai Photo Biennale Foundation
item.description: The CPB Foundation, which runs the Chennai Photo Biennale, opened the third edition of its International Photography Open Call on World Photography Day 2026. It is open to anyone, from anywhere, on any subject, with no age limit, though applicants under 18 need guardian consent. Entries can be single images or a photo series of ten to twenty pictures, and there is no cap on how many entries one photographer may make. The foundation asks for a cohesive body of work rather than a set of unrelated pictures under the series category, and for a concept note or captions with each submission; English is explicitly not a judging criterion. Entries are reviewed by an international jury of curators, institutional directors and industry figures, still to be announced for this edition, and past panels have included Alessia Glaviano of PhotoVogue, Bharat Sikka, Julie Héraut of LE BAL, Gwen Lee of DECK and Michael Weir of Belfast Photo Festival. Selected finalists are printed and exhibited free of charge to them in a large-scale public exhibition spread across Chennai, with the possibility of a travelling show in another Indian city and digital showcases at partner festivals. Two Sigma 35mm f1.4 DG DN Art lenses go to one single-image and one series winner. Notifications are due in late December 2026. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: €8 single image / €15 series (₹300 / ₹700 South Asia, ₹100 / ₹200 students in India). Prize: Camera gear + Exhibition.

item.title: Dublin Art Book Fair 2026 — Artist Book Open Call · Temple Bar Gallery + Studios
item.description: Temple Bar Gallery + Studios runs the open call for the artist book section of Dublin Art Book Fair, which takes place 3 to 13 December 2026. Each year the section gathers books made by contemporary artists, designers and art writers who experiment with the book form and its potential for artistic expression, printed and hand-made alike, turning the fair into a space for the book as a medium in itself. Photobooks and self-published photographic work sit squarely inside that remit. The guest curator for 2026 is the writer, curator and editor Nathan O'Donnell, co-editor of PVA (Journal + Books), who has held commissions from Dublin City Arts Office, the Arts Council, IMMA and Ormston House and was Samuel Beckett Creative Fellow at Trinity College Dublin in 2023. Applications are open to individual artists resident in the Republic of Ireland or Northern Ireland only; organisations, collectives and small presses should contact the gallery separately. You may submit up to three different titles with a maximum of six copies of each, and each title needs up to three images showing the book's physicality. All books must be for sale at a maximum retail price of 40 euro, and the fair deducts 10% commission on sales. Books must withstand unsupervised public handling; the fair is a retail environment rather than an exhibition. Applicants are notified by 20 October 2026. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Tomorrow, Imagined: 17th Annual Patricia Sitar Juried Exhibition · Sitar Arts Center
item.description: Sitar Arts Center's Cafritz Gallery in Washington DC has hosted an annual public juried exhibition for seventeen years, each edition with a new theme. Sitar staff decide which works enter the show and a fresh panel of guest jurors, drawn from practising visual artists and arts professionals across the DC community, judges the awards. Tomorrow, Imagined asks artists to explore what lies ahead: the hopes, questions and possibilities that shape where we are headed as a community and a world. The centre is clear that this is not about predicting what will happen but about asking what future one is imagining and what future one is helping to create, and artists are encouraged to interpret the theme broadly. All mediums are welcome across two-dimensional, three-dimensional and film, video and new media work, and photography is one of the mediums named on the centre's own entry form. AI-generated imagery is not allowed. Open to artists aged 16 and over resident in the United States, with entrants required to be 16 by the date of submission. Prizes run to $450 and $250 for first and second place among adult artists aged 22 and over, $250 and $150 for young adult artists aged 16 to 21, and a $100 People's Choice award. Entry is free for anyone aged 16 to 21 and for Sitar community members up to three pieces; everyone else pays $15 for three works and $5 for each of up to two more. Accepted work is delivered to the centre in January 2027 and the exhibition opens on February 8. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $15 for up to 3 works, $5 each additional (free for ages 16–21). Prize: $450 / $250 / $150 / $100.

item.title: 128th Annual Exhibition by Indiana and Ohio Artists · Richmond Art Museum
item.description: The Richmond Art Museum's annual juried exhibition, endowed in memory of Arthur S. Postle, reaches its 128th edition. Open to artists 18 and over who live in Indiana or Ohio, with original work completed in 2025 or 2026 and not previously shown in a RAM Annual. Both 2-D and 3-D work is eligible and photography is named in the museum's own media list alongside drawing, printmaking, mixed media, painting, fiber arts, clay, jewelry, sculpture, wood and glass. No AI-generated artwork and no AI-generated reference images. Two works per artist, neither over 60 inches in any direction or 50 pounds. Approximately $30,000 in prizes and purchase awards: $5,000 Best of Show, three $1,000 Awards of Excellence, five $500 and six $250 Merit Awards. The jurors are Amy MacLennan, curator at the Swope Art Museum in Terre Haute; Brian Harper, founder of the ceramics nonprofit Artaxis; and photographer Antonio McAfee. An Amateur Division runs beside the Advanced Division for artists in the early stages of their practice, and admits work made under supervision. The museum retains a 30% commission and shows the exhibition November 5, 2026 – January 9, 2027. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $55 ($30 members and students). Prize: ~$30,000 in awards.

item.title: 34th Annual Open Juried Show · Guild of Creative Art
item.description: The Guild of Creative Art's all-media October show, running at its Shrewsbury gallery October 4-28, 2026. Photography is one of three entry categories and is defined tightly: all entries must have originated with a camera, composites may use no one else's frames, stock photography is barred, and any image containing AI-generated content, including Photoshop's generative tools, is disqualified. Up to three works, none over 48 inches on any side including the frame; diptychs and triptychs count as a single entry. The jurors are Jim LaSala, a fine art photographer and managing partner at Xact Studios in Hillsborough, and James Yarosh, artist and owner of James Yarosh Associates Fine Art Gallery in Holmdel. Around $2,300 in cash awards is on offer and six of the named prizes go to photography: $200 Best in Photography plus $100 awards for macro, landscape, nature, people and action work, alongside ten Bronze Achievement medals. Work is hand-delivered on September 30 and the Guild takes a 33 1/3% commission on sales. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: $40 for 1 work ($20 members). Prize: $2,300 in cash awards.

item.title: 47th Biennial Museum Exhibition · Montgomery Art Guild & Montgomery Museum of Fine Arts
item.description: Since 1960 the Montgomery Museum of Fine Arts has partnered with the Montgomery Art Guild on a biennial survey of contemporary regional art in the museum's galleries; this is the 47th edition, on view in the Atrium, Blackmon and Weil Galleries from December 2026 to March 14, 2027. Photographs are named in the organisers' own media list alongside paintings, drawings, prints, sculptures, ceramics, computer graphics, mixed media, fiber art and fine crafts. There is no theme. Open to Alabama residents aged 19 and over, with no membership requirement; up to five works completed in 2024, 2025 or 2026 and not previously shown at the museum. Work made from photographs the artist did not take is barred, and there can be no AI assistance in any part of making the work. Wall pieces may not exceed 44 inches on the longest side including the frame. The juror is Gary Chapman, Professor Emeritus of Painting and Drawing at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, who selects from digital images and picks the award winners from the works on the wall. Over $5,250 has been raised for cash awards so far and neither the guild nor the museum takes a commission on sales. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $15 per work. Prize: $5,250+ in cash awards.

item.title: 55th Annual Juried Art Exhibition · Valley Art Center
item.description: Valley Art Center's annual juried exhibition, a fixture of the Northeast Ohio art calendar for 55 years, shows in the Bowen Gallery in Chagrin Falls from November 6 to December 16, 2026. Artists living within a 250-mile radius of Chagrin Falls may enter up to three works in any medium, and Photography/Prints is one of the eight entry categories alongside textiles, glass and enamel, wood, metal and sculpture, jewelry, painting and drawing, ceramics, and mixed media. The centre usually receives around 400 works and juries down to about 55; this year only one piece per accepted artist will hang, to widen the range of artists and media on the walls. Over $3,500 in cash goes to Best of Show, first, second and third place and several community-sponsored awards. Work does not have to be for sale, and Valley Art Center takes a 40% commission on anything that sells. Entries open on August 26, 2026. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: $15 per work. Prize: $3,500+ in cash awards.

item.title: Call for Submissions — Exhibitions 2027–2028 · Spellerberg Projects
item.description: Spellerberg Projects, an artist-run gallery and studio in Lockhart, Texas, about 40 miles from Austin, is taking proposals for month-long solo and duo exhibitions across 2027 and 2028. The gallery is marking ten years of showing contemporary art and supporting emerging and established artists, and it welcomes submissions in any visual medium from individuals or pairs, though not from larger groups. There is no application fee. Applicants must be based in the United States or due to be during 2027-2028; artists who have exhibited at Spellerberg in the past three years cannot apply, but previous unsuccessful applicants are encouraged to try again. Attending a reception in Lockhart is strongly encouraged but not required. An independent jury of working artists reviews everything and, because the programme spans two years, selections are made on a rolling basis through 2028 rather than on a single decision date, with artists contacted as exhibition dates open up. A separate year-round call covers performances, screenings, workshops, pop-ups and talks in the upstairs space. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Month-long solo or duo exhibition.

item.title: The 9th John Ruskin Prize — Not for Present Delight
item.description: Founded by the Guild of St George in 2012 and managed by Parker Harris under the administrative umbrella of The Big Draw, the John Ruskin Prize is a multidisciplinary art prize open to artists, designers and makers worldwide, amateur or professional, aged 18 and over. The ninth edition takes its theme, Not for Present Delight, from The Seven Lamps of Architecture, where Ruskin urged makers to build for their descendants rather than the present moment: the call asks what it means to create with an awareness of consequence, while also posing the challenge of whether art must serve a purpose beyond itself. Photography is named explicitly among the accepted media, alongside "Photographic Elements, Including Those Manipulated or Collaged" and "Collage, in all materials, including photography"; the prize has honoured photographers in past editions. Work must have been made in the past four years and submissions are judged digitally, with installations, diptychs and triptychs counted as a single artwork. The selection panel shortlists up to 80 artists for an exhibition at Trinity Buoy Wharf in London, running 28 January to 21 February 2027 with an awards evening on 27 January. Four winners share £9,500: a £3,000 first prize from the Guild of St George, the £1,000 Alan Davidson Under 26 Prize, the £3,000 Ruskin Mill Trust Prize for a beautifully crafted functional object, and the £2,500 Chelsea Arts Club Trust Prize for a mid-career artist without gallery representation. A GreatArt People's Choice Award adds £500 of materials. International entrants pay a reduced fee and are not obliged to ship work, showing online and in the catalogue instead. Entrants confirm at submission that the work was created by a human. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: £25 (1 artwork); £20 under 26; £15 international. Prize: £9,500 across four prizes.

item.title: Wings of Hope Bird Photography Contest · Knowing Hope
item.description: Knowing Hope, a US non-profit that funds medical care for children with chronic and catastrophic illness in under-resourced communities across Asia, has launched its first annual bird photography contest as a fundraiser. Photographers of all levels may enter four categories — Birds in Flight, Perched & Portrait, Behavior & Interaction, and Juvenile & Nesting — across two divisions: a novice division for those who have not sold prints, won photography awards or worked professionally, and an advanced division for everyone else. Entries are open to photographers aged 16 and over, with up to ten entries each and one to four photographs per entry; photographs may be spread across any combination of categories. AI-generated images are barred and basic adjustments are allowed, but elements may not be added, removed or substantially altered. Eight category and division winners receive equipment prizes including a Cotton Carrier harness, Vortex binoculars, a Delkin CFexpress card, a Wimberley Monogimbal head, a Think Tank backpack and a KelbyOne Pro membership. Judging is by Duade Paton, an Australian bird photographer and BirdLife Australia contributor; Marina Scarr, whose avian work has appeared in National Wildlife, Nature's Best Photography and Living Bird; and David Lindo, The Urban Birder, a judge for Bird Photographer of the Year and the British Wildlife Photography Awards. Each photograph is scored 1–5 on technical quality, composition and artistic merit, moment and impact, and overall impression. Photographers keep full copyright, granting the organisers a non-exclusive licence for promotional and fundraising use with credit. Winners are announced between 1 and 14 November 2026. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $15–$50 by photo count. Prize: Photography gear for 8 winners.

item.title: Refusing Rehearsing Resisting · VBKÖ – Austrian Association of Women Artists
item.description: VBKÖ, the Austrian Association of Wom*n Artists founded in Vienna in 1910, invites proposals for its annual programme running March 2027 to February 2028. Following feminist, queer, anti-racist, anti-colonial and anti-authoritarian traditions, the call asks for projects that nurture communal care and build a platform for collective rehearsals imagining alternative futures — work that allows for tenderness, is not afraid of ugly feelings, and holds different truths. Proposals must bring together multiple artists, collectives or collaborative practices; solo exhibitions and single-artist presentations are not supported. Exhibition formats activated by public programming — screenings, performances, workshops, lectures — are encouraged. Each selected project receives a total budget of €4,000 covering artist fees and production, plus the VBKÖ space and shared kitchen, graphic design of promotional material, press announcements, photo documentation, up to 10 hours of technical support and use of the house technical equipment. Projects run 4 to 6 weeks. Applicants based outside Vienna must cover travel, accommodation and shipping from the project budget or external funding; VBKÖ provides invitation and support letters to help secure it. Applications go by email as a single PDF with a programme description, CVs for all participants, a financial plan based on Fair Pay principles, and three high-resolution images. Selected proposals are announced at the beginning of October 2026. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €4,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Black Whimsy — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City, curated by Adesewa Adekoya, opening October 16, 2026. Black Whimsy asks what happens when Black imagination has no limits, inviting artists to picture the ethereal, fantastical and otherworldly possibilities of Black life and creativity across the diaspora — the many surreal and dreamlike worlds in which Black people can exist — and to escape reality for a while. Open to artists of any age, skill level or background; all art is accepted except corporate logos, personal advertising and video, and still JPEGs only, so photographic work is eligible. Selected works are displayed on NYC ad space for at least one month; artists are notified after September 21, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in NYC.

item.title: Slow Digestion — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City, curated by Jude Griebel, opening October 23, 2026. Slow Digestion sets out to subvert the billboard as corporate ad space that normalises ultra-processed food, inviting work on harvesting, factory farming, the unseen labour behind agriculture, and food histories embedded in communities and private kitchens. The organisers want artworks that treat eating as a storied, reflective, personal and sometimes disquieting act — pieces that can be slowly digested by the public in spaces built to promote rapid consumption. Open to artists of any age, skill level or background; all art is accepted except corporate logos, personal advertising and video, and still JPEGs only, so photographic work is eligible. Artists are notified after September 28, 2026 and selected work is on view for at least one month. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in NYC.

item.title: CURRENTS · Photographic Center Northwest
item.description: Shutter & Light Collective and Photographic Center Northwest present CURRENTS, a group exhibition exploring the versatility of analog photography and the photography culture growing throughout the Northwest. Work is welcomed from across the analog spectrum — scanned film, darkroom prints, instant film, pinhole, direct-positive processes, cyanotypes, alternative and experimental processes, and multimedia — and the show is curated through analog process, visual style and storytelling. There is no required subject matter and the theme is open. Artists may submit up to five works or series; prints should generally be no larger than 16 × 20 inches, and alternative presentations and unframed work are considered on request. Artists are responsible for printing and framing, with guidance offered by the organisers. The $3 fee is described as cost recovery only, with no-questions-asked waivers for artists facing financial or access barriers, and sales carry a voluntary 20% commission. Attendance at the November 12 opening is required of participating local artists. Exhibition runs November 2 – December 16, 2026 at PCNW in Seattle. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $3 (fee waivers available). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Streets · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on street photography in all its registers - the photographer moving through public life as both observer and participant, attentive to gesture, chance, humour, tension and the fleeting relationships between people and place. Praxis seeks work that explores the streets from all angles, including people, public spaces, urban structures and documentary subject matter, in black and white or colour, traditional or experimental. The juror is Jonathan Pavlica. Up to 74 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (17 October - 14 November 2026) and featured on the gallery's online exhibition page. Awards are a Juror's Choice (free entry into three future calls), a Directors' Choice (two future calls) and eight honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, printed catalogue and online gallery. Images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Colorscapes · Photo Artfolio
item.description: Global online exhibition from Photo Artfolio exploring the expressive power of colour in photography - bold saturated hues, subtle palettes and quiet tonal relationships, from the unexpected collision of colours on a city street to the shifting tones of a landscape, a portrait defined by its palette, or an abstract composition built entirely around colour, light and form. Open to all photographic genres and approaches, including documentary, portraiture, street, landscape, nature, architecture, still life, conceptual, fine art and experimental work. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers; all work must be original and made by the submitting photographer, and AI-generated imagery is not eligible. Up to 20 images may be entered, at $20 for the first image and $5 for each additional one. Cash prizes of $500, $350 and $150, and all accepted photographs are shown in the online exhibition, which opens on 11 November 2026. Photo Artfolio's own site has not yet posted this cycle's prospectus, so the full prospectus and the entry route are on the CaFE listing linked here. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: $20 + $5 each additional image. Prize: $500 + $350 + $150.

item.title: Street Photographers Foundation Awards 2026
item.description: The Street Photographers Foundation's annual awards, open worldwide to professionals, students and enthusiasts alike, for photographs made on the street in the broadest sense of the word - mobile and analogue, conceptual and documentary, street portraits, urban, street fashion, road trips, street art, travel, architecture, abstract, graphic and large format. As the foundation puts it, the tools you use are not important. Entries are made either as a single photograph judged on its own or as a series of four to ten photographs judged together as one work. The 2026 jury is Chloe Coleman (photo editor at the Washington Post), Cheryl Dunn, Mary-Irene Marek of Leica Camera, foundation founder Masoud Gharaei, Magnum photographer Richard Kalvar and Stefano Mirabella of the Italian Street Photo Festival. First prizes of €1,000 go to the strongest single image and to the strongest series, each exhibited and given a featured article, and fifteen Jurors' Picks are selected for the exhibition. Photographers retain full copyright, entries stay private until results are announced, and winning work travels - the 2020 and 2021 awards became an exhibition of 62 photographs by 43 photographers at Galerie Joseph Le Palais in Paris. Photographs are accepted regardless of when they were taken. Entrants must be 18 or over, and for compliance reasons entries cannot be accepted from Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria or the regions of Crimea, Luhansk and Donetsk. A limited number of discretionary single-photo fee waivers is available to photographers who genuinely cannot afford the entry fee. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: €10 per single image, €45 per series. Prize: €1,000 single + €1,000 series + exhibition.

item.title: 22nd International Alternative Processes Competition · Soho Photo Gallery
item.description: Soho Photo Gallery's 22nd International Alternative Processes Competition, the annual juried show devoted to historic and handmade photographic processes at New York's longest-running co-operative photography gallery. Accepted processes include, but are not limited to, albumen, cyanotype, Van Dyke brown, platinum/palladium, gum bichromate, bromoil, salt print, tintype, ziatype, daguerreotype, image transfers, liquid emulsion, anthotypes, photogravure and chemigrams, as well as handmade prints made from digital negatives - the gallery's rule is that the image must originate in an alternative process and must not be AI-generated. There is no limitation on subject matter, and no image may measure more than 40 inches on its longest side. The juror is Amy Arbus, who photographed downtown New York for The Village Voice from 1980 to 1990 (the work that became On the Street 1980-1990), has published The Inconvenience of Being Born and The Fourth Wall, has taught at the International Center of Photography and Maine Media Workshops, and whose prints are held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, MoMA and the New York Public Library. Selected work is exhibited at the gallery's West 23rd Street space in Chelsea from 2 to 20 December 2026, with an opening reception on 3 December. Prizes are $300, $200 and $100 plus four honourable mentions, and the gallery takes 30% commission on sales during the show. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over, excluding Soho Photo Gallery members. Note that sohophoto.com's own competition page has not yet been rolled over from the 2025 edition - the current prospectus, dates and juror are on the CaFE listing linked here. — Deadline: September 23, 2026. Fee: $45 for 5 images, $5 per additional image up to 15. Prize: $300 / $200 / $100 + exhibition.
